title: The Late Glasshouse
premise: Xanthe Marchetti, a piano tuner who reads a house's history through its radiators and pipes, has spent thirty years as the invisible caretaker of Glasshouse, the decaying estate of the family that once employed their mother. When demolition notices arrive and a box of undelivered letters surfaces behind a wardrobe, Xanthe learns that the letters were written by their mother to the house's late matriarch—and that Xanthe's own birth was the scandal that broke the household apart. As they track down the surviving Marchetti relatives, each holding a different version of the truth, Xanthe must decide whether belonging can be claimed or only given. In the end, with the wreckers scheduled at dawn, Xanthe plays the house's untuned piano one last time, forgives the stranger in the photographs—their mother—and chooses to let Glasshouse fall while carrying its memory forward as heir rather than servant.
about_author: Sable Thackeray is a former architectural conservator who spent a decade documenting buildings slated for demolition before turning to fiction. They live in a converted glasshouse on the Yorkshire coast, where they write about inheritance, houses, and the people who keep them.

chapters.title: The Tuner's Ear
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine tuning visit establishes Xanthe's uncanny ability to hear a building's history in its pipes and radiators, and their practiced smile that ends conversations. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Notice of Demolition
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A letter arrives: Glasshouse, where Xanthe has lived and worked for decades under a loose arrangement with the absent Vane family, will be demolished in six weeks. Emotional beat: the ground shifting beneath an unexamined life.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Packing begins; a wardrobe shifts and reveals a cavity containing a box of letters, all addressed to 'E. Vane' in handwriting Xanthe recognizes too well—their mother's. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: What the Radiators Remember
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, interwoven with the first letter. The letters describe a friendship between Xanthe's mother, Rosa, and Eleanor Vane—until an abrupt stop. Xanthe realizes the house has been keeping a secret in its walls. Emotional beat: hunger for the past.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Flashback chapter to young Xanthe learning invisibility from Rosa, who worked at Glasshouse and taught her child never to be seen. Emotional beat: tenderness laced with resentment toward a protective lie.

chapters.title: A Visitor in Overalls
chapters.summary: Dual POV introducing Dev, a surveyor cataloguing Glasshouse for demolition, who treats the house—and Xanthe—with unexpected attention. Their questions about the property unsettle Xanthe's careful silence. Emotional beat: wary first contact.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A letter reveals Rosa was pregnant when she left Glasshouse suddenly; Eleanor's replies were never sent because someone intercepted them. Xanthe suspects the butler, Aldous, who raised them after Rosa vanished. Emotional beat: suspicion corroding grief.

chapters.title: Aldous's Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe visits the dying Aldous in a care home. He deflects with old-world courtesy, but lets slip that Eleanor Vane is still alive, living incognito in Whitby. Emotional beat: the cost of loyalty and lies.

chapters.title: Whitby
chapters.summary: Xanthe travels to find Eleanor, now an elderly woman named Mrs. Grey. She refuses to see them, but her granddaughter Cass watches Xanthe leave with open curiosity. Emotional beat: rejection reopening old wounds.

chapters.title: Cass
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass, researching her grandmother's past for a family history, tracks Xanthe down. Two strangers compare fragments and realize the Vane family story has a deliberate hole shaped like Rosa Marchetti. Emotional beat: alliance forming across class lines.

chapters.title: The Photographs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Among Eleanor's effects Cass finds photographs: Rosa at the piano, Rosa laughing with Eleanor, Rosa visibly pregnant—and a man neither can identify standing at the edge of every frame. Emotional beat: the stranger in the pictures becomes personal.

chapters.title: Dev's Report
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev discovers the demolition order was pushed through by a developer connected to the Vane estate's trustees—someone inside the family wants Glasshouse gone quickly. Emotional beat: rising stakes, power moving behind closed doors.

chapters.title: The Man at the Edge
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the photograph trail, Xanthe identifies the recurring figure: Marcus Vane, Eleanor's brother, presumed dead abroad. Records show he returned quietly years ago and now controls the trust. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into certainty.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass confronts Marcus at a trustee dinner and is warned off with chilling politeness; her access to family archives is revoked. Emotional beat: power showing its teeth, corruption revealed as inheritance itself.

chapters.title: Rosa's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The final unsent letter reveals the truth: Marcus fathered Xanthe, then forced Rosa out to protect his reputation while Eleanor's protests went unheard. Xanthe learns their whole identity was engineered by another man's shame. Emotional beat: devastation and strange liberation.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Trust
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe confronts Marcus, who offers money and continued anonymity in exchange for silence. For the first time, Xanthe refuses the smile and speaks plainly. Emotional beat: claiming voice over invisibility.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Door
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Cass return to Whitby armed with the last letter. Eleanor, frail but lucid, finally opens the door and admits she searched for Rosa for years—interception she blamed herself for. Emotional beat: forgiveness beginning as recognition.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Demolition is dawn; legal appeals fail against Marcus's influence. Xanthe returns to Glasshouse alone, listening one last time to every radiator, every pipe, the house telling its whole story at last. Emotional beat: elegy and resolve.

chapters.title: The Untuned Piano
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. At midnight, Xanthe plays the long-silent piano deliberately badly, then beautifully, letting the house hear itself. Cass and Dev arrive uninvited and stay. Emotional beat: communion; belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The wreckers come. Xanthe stands at the gate beside Cass, Dev, and—unexpectedly—Eleanor in a wheelchair, watching Marcus arrive to gloat and finding nothing to say to him. Emotional beat: release; the house falls, the hold breaks.

chapters.title: Heirloom
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Weeks later, Cass publishes the true family history; Marcus's reputation curdles without a trial. Xanthe receives the box of letters, formally, as inheritance. Emotional beat: justice as quiet reordering, not spectacle.

chapters.title: Tuning Fork
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe takes work tuning pianos along the coast, no longer hiding behind the smile, the letters carried in a satchel like a heartbeat. In a stranger's front room, they hear a new house begin to speak. Emotional beat: identity integrated; belonging carried within.
